messages:
Sarah K: quick idea — can we add a single 'deploy braid' bot command that wires pin, smoke, release-note gen, and canary split into one atomic flow?
Noah P: curious, what does braid do different from current pin+canary scripts?
Sarah K: instead of separate steps, braid would: 1) pin model/version, 2) run smoke suite, 3) attach changelog template and post release note draft, 4) kick canary with configurable % and rollback hooks.
Leo M: sounds useful. How would users opt into safety windows?
Sarah K: braid would respect change-window tags and reject if outside allowed window unless --force-with-approval passed. Also add auto-schedule to queue for next window.
Maria S: can we see a stub of the command syntax?
Sarah K: sure, PoC snippet I tossed together:
```
# run in infractl or via /deploy-bot
deploy-braid --svc web --version v2026-03-21-rc1 
            --smoke-suite smoke/quick-1m 
            --canary 10 --canary-duration 15m 
            --notes-template templates/release_minimal.md
            --auto-rollback-on-failure
```
Noah P: neat. what's the smoke-suite contract? unit tests or e2e?
Leo M: short smoke should be a thin polymer of healthchecks + a 3-request flow against staging. Takes <60s. Full e2e stays separate.
Sarah K: right — braid defaults to quick checks, but supports longer suites via --smoke-suite. Also supports a --dry-run that prints all steps and generated notes.
Maria S: does deploy-bot support interactive approvals? we need manager signoff for >50% canary.
Sarah K: yes — braid integrates with /deploy-bot approve workflows. If canary >50 then it pauses and posts an approval thread to the channel.
deploy-bot: INFO: queued braid job 8732 for svc=web version=v2026-03-21-rc1. awaiting smoke results.
Noah P: error handling? how do we rollback if smoke fails mid-run?
Sarah K: braid will run smoke before traffic shift. If smoke fails: auto-unpin and abort, post rollback summary. If failure after canary shift, it triggers configured rollback hooks and optional immediate full rollback.
Leo M: what about release notes? can braid pull PR descriptions and changelog snippets?
Maria S: we should auto-generate notes from merged PRs between previous pinned tag and new tag, with a short template, then open a draft in #release-notes for edits.
Sarah K: implemented in PoC — it calls git log between tags, groups by PR label, and fills template. Example output: 
```
- Fix: API timeout regression (PR #412)
- Perf: reduce KV cache miss for reroute (PR #398)
- Ops: add pinflow telemetry (PR #401)
```
Noah P: can we make braid produce a small JSON artifact with steps, checks, and metrics for auditing?
Sarah K: yes — braid emits run metadata to /releases/artifacts and to our observability so we can later reconstruct what happened.
Leo M: who wants to own turning PoC into a real bot command? I can pick up the smoke orchestration and rollback hooks.
Maria S: I'll do the release-note templater and git integration.
Noah P: I'll wire the change-window evaluation and approval gating.
Sarah K: awesome — I'll stub the CLI args, permission checks, and help text. Plan: small RFC in eng-releases next week, then a 2-sprint implementation.
Maria S: can we add a tiny UX shim so the bot posts a condensed checklist like: pinned, smoke ok, notes posted, canary started? makes oncall life easier. :thumbsup:
Sarah K: yes — summary checkboxes are default.
Noah P: sounds good. Filing a tracking ticket now and linking the PoC gist.
Sarah K: thanks — rough action items in thread pinned to the ticket.
Maria S: ack.
Leo M: ack.
